name: The St. Regis Bahia Beach Resort
positioning: Oceanfront St. Regis resort in Rio Grande, Puerto Rico, on a two-mile beach, set on a former sugar cane and coconut farm that is now a certified Audubon sanctuary
best_for: Beach and nature lovers who want birdlife and a turtle conservation program on site
Golfers, with a Robert Trent Jones Jr.-designed course
Families, with the Tortuga Kid's Club

facts.text: The resort was built on a former sugar cane and coconut farm and originally opened in 2010.
Pathways wind through manicured gardens and open onto an expansive two-mile-long beach.
Rooms were designed by local designer Nono Maldonado in dolphin-gray and sand-dollar-white, with terraces.
Bathrooms have rain showers and soaking tubs.
Seagrapes is the casual poolside restaurant, and Paros is the upscale Mediterranean restaurant.
The lobby bar serves a local spin on the Bloody Mary with crushed plantain chips.
The Iridium spa has a Jacuzzi, steam rooms, cold pools, a sauna, and yoga and Pilates classes.
Besides a curving pool and a Robert Trent Jones Jr.-designed golf course, the resort has a boathouse for kayaking and paddleboarding, and pickleball courts.
The resort has the Tortuga Kid's Club.
El Yunque rainforest is a 20-minute drive away, and lakes for boating and fishing are about 10 minutes away.

highlights.text: The property is a certified Audubon sanctuary, so guests can look out for Puerto Rican parrots and other exotic birds.
The resort hosts a program to rehabilitate the Leatherback Turtle population.
The lobby bar displays 'The Long Awaited Voyage,' a mural by local artist Arnaldo Roche Rabell.
The spa's massage villas incorporate rum, coffee and tropical fruits into treatments.
The resort holds a nightly Champagne sabering.

considerations.text: The hotel is a 35-minute drive from SJU airport.
WhataHotel notes the remote location means travel time to explore Puerto Rico's attractions.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing reflecting the premium positioning.
